comparison.objective: PR-717 grates cheese while holding a box grater steady; the candidate adjusts and locks a shock absorber and tunes its stopping behavior.
comparison.physical_skill: Both use bimanual counterholding during forceful motion. PR-717 requires sustained surface contact and repeated rubbing strokes; the candidate requires precise hex-socket engagement, captive setscrew operation, fine collar rotation, relocking, and impact-response iteration.
comparison.success_condition: PR-717 requires ≥18 cm of valid rubbing with the grater upright, cheese put down, and arms returned. The candidate requires two safe repeatable carriage stops and verified lock retention. Candidate rebound, overload, drift, and witness-torque thresholds remain undeclared, but they do not resemble the grating-distance rubric.
comparison.reason: Shared stabilization is generic; abrasive reciprocation and dynamic damper commissioning have different mechanisms, tested abilities, and terminal outcomes.
